proof_checks: ConvexOn univ converts to StrongConvexOn modulus0. Actual gradient monotonicity is derived via StrongConvexFirstOrder from C2-derived differentiability; ConvexityC2.gradient_mono_iff_fderiv2_lower then supplies the genuine Hessian diagonal nonnegativity. No Hessian positivity is assumed.

R is the continuous linear inverse real Riesz map. H x = R.comp of actual fderiv(fderiv f) at x. C2 gives C1 fderiv; chain rule proves HasFDerivAt gradient f (H x) x. toDual_symm_apply gives inner(Hx v,v)=D2f(x)[v,v]; no unrelated gradient/Hessian representative or symmetry assumption supplied.
First-order lower support at x and z, after reversing z-x, correctly gives f(x)-f(z)<=inner(gradient f x,x-z). This sign is then used in both Lyapunov derivative and value rate.

Actual right gradient ODE is composed with genuine gradient derivative, objective derivative, and displacement derivative. norm_sq yields factor2 and inner order is correctly exchanged with real_inner_comm.

Product rules cancel +2t normgradient squared against -2t normgradient squared. D(t)=-2t^2 inner(Hg,g)+2gap-2inner(g,X-z). Hessian nonnegativity and first-order support make D(t)<=0. No gap sign needed at this derivative step.

Continuity of L on closed Icc is derived from derivative-derived gradient continuity and supplied X continuity. Gronwall K=epsilon=0 applies on each [a,b] subset [0,T]; right derivative points u<b imply u<T even when b=T. It yields true AntitoneOn, not merely L(t)<=L(0).

At positive t, global minimum supplies gap>=0 and squared displacement>=0. Dropping these potential terms and dividing by t^2>0 yields gradient squared<=initial squared distance/t^2 with coefficient1.

First-order support followed by Cauchy gives gap<=normgradient*normdistance. Multiplication by t>=0 and Young via (t*normgradient-normdistance)^2>=0 yield2t gap<=t^2 normgradient squared+distance squared. Combined with L bound gives4t gap<=initial distance squared; division by4t>0 gives exact1/4 coefficient.

Antitone statement includes both endpoints and T=0. At T=0 ODE premises range over empty Ico, antitonicity is on a singleton, and both normalized conclusions range over empty Ioc. No finite t=0 quotient is asserted. No derivative at T or negative time is used.
